newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maybank says Kwong Yik price satisfactory.
newsitem.headline: Maybank says Kwong Yik price satisfactory.

text.p: Malaysia's largest banking group, Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), said on Tuesday its selling price of 8.80 ringgit per share for its subsidiary Kwong Yik Bank Bhd was "the right price".
"We feel that 8.80 ringgit is the right kind of price (for Kwong Yik)," said Maybank managing director Amirsham Aziz.
The sale of Kwong Yik would also maximise the bank's value to Maybank, he told a news conference.
Malaysian top stockbroker Rashid Hussain Bhd said earlier on Tuesday it had bought Maybank's 75 percent stake in Kwong Yik for a total of 2.16 billion ringgit.
Amirsham said another rationale for the sale was that the growth of Maybank's own operations "would not require the call of additional capital", he said.
The sale would bring an extraordinary gain of about 1.87 billion ringgit for Maybank for the year ended June 30, 1997.
Amirsham said Kwong Yik did not add to his bank's market presence as Maybank -- being Malaysia's largest banking group -- had already diversified into every corporate and commercial financial sector.
"Our strategy is in all aspects, so adding Kwong Yik will not add to our strength," he added.
Amirsham said the bank would continue to expand into financial services sector in Malaysia, but added this plan was unlikely to include the acquisition of another commmercial bank.
"But if there are any other opportunities for acquisitions within the sector, we will look at it," he said.
The bank would also use proceeds from the sale of Kwong Yik to help in its expansion into Southeast Asia, he said.

Maybank has said it was eyeing to buy a controlling stake in a Philippines bank, and is seeking to expand its operations in Thailand and Indonesia. A joint venture in Burma is also being looked at, Amirsham said.
